title: Morgiana and the Forty Thieves
text:
Ali Baba, a poor woodcutter, saw forty thieves open a cave in a rock with the words "Open, Sesame" and helped himself to some of their gold. His greedy brother Cassim went to the cave, forgot the password on the way out, and was killed by the thieves. Ali Baba secretly brought his body home, and the family's clever slave girl, Morgiana, arranged for a cobbler to be led there blindfolded to sew it together, so the death could pass as natural.

The thieves knew someone else had their secret. One of them found the cobbler, had himself led to the house, and marked its door with chalk. Morgiana noticed the mark and put the same mark on every door in the street. That night the thieves could not tell which house it was. A second thief marked the door with red chalk, and again she marked all the neighbors' doors.

Then the captain came himself, disguised as an oil merchant, with mules carrying large jars. One held oil; in the others hid his men. Going to fetch oil for a lamp, Morgiana heard a voice from a jar and discovered the plot. She boiled oil and poured it into each jar, killing the men inside. The captain escaped, but later returned in disguise as a guest. Morgiana recognized him, performed a dance with a dagger, and killed him. Ali Baba gave her her freedom and married her to his son.
lesson: Watchfulness beats numbers. Notice the small signs others miss, and answer a clever move with one that makes it useless.
people: Morgiana, Ali Baba, Cassim, the captain of the thieves
location: Persia, in the story; published in France
source: Antoine Galland, Les Mille et une nuits, volume 11 (1717)
caveat: No Arabic manuscript of this tale predates Galland's French version, which he wrote down from a story told to him by Hanna Diyab.
